working_definition: Pm4 is a proximal medullary amacrine neuron of the adult Drosophila optic lobe, arborising at the proximal surface of the medulla predominantly in layers M8-M9 and covering approximately 10-20 columns. It is GABAergic, has no primary axon, and belongs to the Notch OFF hemilineage of secondary neurons born from medulla neuroblasts during the Hth/Opa temporal window. There are approximately 75-85 of these neurons per hemisphere.

best_match.fbbt_definition: Proximal medullary amacrine neuron that branches at the proximal surface of the medulla. It covers around 10-20 columns with its pre- and post-synapses mostly in layers M8-M9 (Nern et al., 2025). It occupies a central intracolumnar position. It is GABAergic (Davis et al., 2020). There are around 75-85 of these neurons per hemisphere (Nern et al., 2025).

justification: The FBbt term 'proximal medullary amacrine neuron Pm4' (FBbt:00111282) was returned as the top hit on an exact-label search for 'Pm4' in FBbt and is not obsolete. Its definition precisely matches every defining feature of the cluster: proximal medulla location, M8-M9 layer arborisation, 10-20 column spread, GABAergic neurotransmitter identity, amacrine morphology, and approximate cell count per hemisphere. The cluster label 'Pm4' is the canonical anatomical subtype name used in optic-lobe nomenclature, not a marker or driver name, so label and definition align directly. The immature form FBbt:00052323 was noted but rejected as the atlas captures adult cells (scRNAseq of adult optic lobe).

other_candidates.reason_rejected: Denotes the immature (pupal/larval) form; the Kurmangaliyev 2020 atlas profiles adult Drosophila optic-lobe cells, so the adult term FBbt:00111282 is the correct match.
